newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa stocks end 1996 in firm mood.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa stocks end 1996 in firm mood.

text.p: South African shares ended 1996 in a firm mood as buoyant international markets and the unit trust close-out gave prices a lift, dealers said on Tuesday.

They said positive sentiment from recent record highs in London and New York was still supporting South African stocks and also pointed to a degree of price manipulation as unit trusts sought to boost their books before the end of the year.
The final session of the year ended early at noon (1000GMT) as traders prepared for New Year's Eve festivities, but volumes were a healthy 218 million rands worth of shares.
The all-share index closed at 6,657.5, up 29.1 points, as industrials ticked up 34.7 points to 7,921.6.
Dealers said the rise was likely to continue when trade resumes on Thursday.
The gold market was quiet as the bullion price rose a fraction in early European trade. But most gold shares rose as dealers foresaw a break through the psychologically important $370 an ounce level.
The golds index firmed 5.4 points to 1,506.2.
